Texture Generator: procedural sprites, VFX and packed masks

Stable Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-20

Bake one texture at a time — a leaf, a feather, a flame, a packed RGBA mask — with the Texture Generator node graph.

The Texture Generator is a node graph that bakes one texture: a leaf, a feather, a flame, a shock ring, a packed RGBA mask. It is a tool of its own, next to the Material Generator, because the two jobs differ.

Material Generator Texture Generator
Produces a PBR material (.mat plus base, normal, ORM, emissive maps) a single image, with alpha
Result node Output (Color, Roughness, Metallic, Height, AO, Emissive, Opacity, Normal) Texture Output (Colour + alpha, or packed R, G, B, A)
Tiling seamless optional: an object sits in the image with a transparent margin
Preview engine sphere or plane with real lighting checkerboard, plus single-channel views
File <material>.generator.material beside the .mat <name>.generator.texture in Textures/, with the .png
Library 85 materials 21 textures: foliage, organic, fire and smoke, effects, procedural, data
Accent colour cyan orange (title bar and the Texture Output node)

They can feed each other (bake a flame to a PNG and use it as an emissive map), but a texture graph never opens as a material and vice versa: the loaders refuse the other format.

Images are produced headless by the engine tooling; the commands to regenerate them are at the end.

1. What is shared and what is not#

Both tools run on the same engine room, so every improvement to one helps the other:

  • the node store and evaluator (generators::MaterialGraph is only the container of nodes and links, evaluated lazily with a memo);
  • the procedural library in uikit/procedural/ (139 ops: 129 for materials plus 10 new VFX & Shapes ops);
  • the node canvas, the parameter editor (sliders, colour pickers, dropdowns generated from each op's table row) and the undo history.

What is separate: the .texgraph format (uikit/texture_graph.rs), the TextureOutput node, the palette, the presets, the panel (panels/texture_generator.rs), the editor state and messages (windows/main/texturegen.rs), the ids (texturegen.*) and the agent actions. The material palette no longer offers the VFX & Shapes ops, and the texture palette hides the PBR Output, image readers and normal-map nodes.

2. The Texture Output node#

Mode Ports Use
Colour + alpha Color, Alpha sprites, leaves, decals. Without an Alpha input the colour's own alpha is kept, which is how the VFX & Shapes ops mask themselves.
Packed channels (RGBA) R, G, B, A data and VFX textures: four greyscale masks in one file. Unconnected R, G and B are 0, A is 1.

Changing the mode drops links to ports that no longer exist. The node cannot be deleted: it is the graph's result. Output goes to a PNG of 8 or 16 bits with straight alpha.

3. VFX & Shapes nodes#

Ten ops, in uikit/procedural/vfx.rs. None is tileable: each draws an object. Colour outputs carry the object's mask in alpha, and the RGB is kept under the transparent area so mip-maps do not gain dark halos. Everything is deterministic for a seed.

Op Makes Outputs Notable parameters
Leaf silhouette from a width profile, midrib and curved side veins Color, Mask, Veins, Height half width, tip sharpness, base roundness, serration, teeth, bend, side veins, vein sweep, texture
Feather vane with barbs, splits and a shaft Color, Mask, Barbs width, vane curve, barbs, slant, splits, bend
Droplet teardrop (smooth union of a circle and a tapered cone) Color, Mask, Dome radius, tail, join smoothing, highlight, tilt
Shockwave Ring distorted ring with an inner glow Color, Value radius, thickness, softness, distortion, noise scale
Flame warped teardrop eroded by noise, fire ramp Color, Intensity, Core width, height, turbulence, stretch, sharpness, phase
Smoke Puff turbulent soft puff Color, Value radius, turbulence, density, softness, phase
Sparks streaking embers with a hot head Color, Value count, length, thickness, radial bias, glow
Radial Burst rays with random lengths and a core Color, Value rays, sharpness, reach, length variation, core size
Soft Glow elliptical falloff Color, Value radius, falloff power, intensity, aspect
Colour Ramp (LUT) 1D gradient along X, Y or radially, four stops Color, Position direction, stops B and C, smooth blend

The ops combine with everything else in the library: the Explosion Burst preset is a burst, a ring and a glow added together and mapped through a Gradient Map, with the sum also wired to the Alpha port.

4. Library#

The Library dropdown replaces the graph with one of 21 presets (one undo step; your size is kept). They are normal graphs, so you can keep editing them.

Category Presets
Foliage Green Leaf, Autumn Leaf, Willow Leaf, Petal Pink / White / Yellow (the Nature Generator uses them for flowers)
Organic Blue Feather, Down Feather, Water Droplet
Fire & Smoke Torch Flame, Blue Flame, Smoke Puff, Dark Smoke
Effects Spark Shower, Shock Ring, Magic Glow, Explosion Burst
Procedural Wave Function Collapse Bricks, Diamond-Square Clouds (both from the Variation class, see the materials guide)
Data Fire Colour Ramp (a 1D LUT), Packed VFX Masks (R smoke, G burst, B glow, A flame)

5. Preview#

The preview is baked at 256 px after every edit (node thumbnails at 96 px), so it follows sliders live. It is drawn over a checkerboard, so transparency is visible. The chips switch the view:

Over checker Colour Alpha R, G, B
the real result RGB with no alpha the mask as grey one channel as grey, for packed masks
Alpha Colour

6. Saving and exporting#

Files go to <project assets>/Textures/ (an existing textures/ is reused; Textures/ relative to the working directory without a project). Export runs on a worker thread, so a 16-bit or flipbook bake does not freeze the editor, and the new image appears in Assets when it finishes:

Button Writes
Save <name>.texgraph, the editable graph (CAFTEXGRAPH1, same text format as material graphs)
Export PNG <name>.png at the chosen size and bit depth; the graph is saved with it so the image can always be edited again
Export flipbook <name>_flipbook_<C>x<R>.png, a sheet of C x R frames

Flipbooks. Flame and Smoke Puff have a Phase parameter that loops from 0 to 1. The flipbook bakes the graph once per frame, advancing every phase parameter in the graph from 0 to just under 1, and lays the frames out row by row; the last frame leads back into the first. A graph without a phase parameter gives identical frames. Frames are size pixels square, so a 4 x 2 sheet at 128 is 512 x 256.

7. For agents and scripts#

Command line (no window):

bash
doppio-material bake-texture --list                                  # presets
doppio-material bake-texture "Torch Flame" --out /tmp/tex --size 512 --bits 16
doppio-material bake-texture "Torch Flame" --out /tmp/tex --size 128 --flipbook 4x2
doppio-material bake-texture my.texgraph --out /tmp/tex
doppio-material bake-texture --all --out /tmp/tex --size 256

MCP (--features agent): query texture_generator (name, size, nodes, links, preset names); actions texture_generator_apply_preset { name }, texture_generator_configure { name | bits | size | flipbook: [c, r] } and texture_generator_export { flipbook?: true }. Everything is a Message, so an agent can do no more than the UI.

Headless driver: fixture texture shows the tab, with preset naming a texture preset (Torch Flame); the flow tests/ui-flows/texture-generator.json covers it.

8. Limits and next steps#

  • The preview is CPU-evaluated at 256 px; exports go up to 2048 px (a 4 x 4 flipbook at 512 is a 2048 px sheet).
  • PNG only: float / EXR output for heightmaps and LUTs is not implemented.
  • The Texture Generator has no image-reader node yet, so it cannot read project bitmaps.
  • The Reseed button gives every seeded node a new seed (a variation of the preset, one undo step); colour variation is still edited in the node properties.
  • A tiled export mode (seamless textures) is not offered: use the Material Generator for tiles.

9. Regenerating the images#

bash
./scripts/capture-texture-docs.sh         # headless UI screenshots (tab, preview modes, graphs)
./scripts/render-texture-gallery.sh       # bakes every preset and two flipbooks (needs ImageMagick)

The UI screenshots come from the headless driver (see headless-testing.md); the flow is caffeine-website/captures/flows/capture-texture-docs.json.
